A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KBLaM and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The earlier Appendices C–F are retained as E–H in v2, alongside new Appendices C and D, allowing reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B report original retrieval, question-answering, refusal, memory-use and ablation results on synthetic and Enron knowledge bases.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds BM25 retrieval comparisons, perturbed-query experiments and RAG efficiency measurements in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The sentence encoder, linear adapters, rectangular attention, attention-score scaling and instruction-tuning objective remain unchanged. Explaining that C=100 matches the largest training KB clarifies an existing choice; the perturbation experiment explicitly uses the same trained model.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds a synthetic-query scenario in which entity names differ from their corresponding KB names, testing retrieval beyond exact name matching. The original synthetic and Enron datasets and question-answering tasks are retained.

E2.justification: v2 introduces two substantive comparisons absent from v1: BM25 for top-1/top-5 retrieval accuracy in Figure 10, and RAG for latency and memory in Figure 11. The existing in-context and zero-shot comparisons remain; RAG is not added as a question-answering quality baseline.

E3.justification: Existing training and evaluation settings are retained. New protocols include GPT-4 perturbation of query entity names and a time-to-first-token/memory benchmark averaged over 40 random synthetic queries, assuming negligible RAG retrieval overhead and including a five-retrieved-triple reference.

E4.justification: Figure 10b adds a robustness test asking whether retrieval survives mismatches between query and KB entity names without retraining. The encoder-capacity, injection-frequency and layerwise analyses in Appendix B remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds with 100 questions per run and retain Figure 6b's standard errors over those seeds. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced. Figure 11's 40 queries specify an evaluation sample size, not additional seeds.

E6.justification: Figures 10–11 substantially extend the results while existing plots and sample answers remain unchanged. BM25 provides stronger Enron retrieval, while KBLaM has better top-1 accuracy under name perturbation. The new efficiency results show faster first-token generation and approximately equal memory to five-triple RAG at 512 KB triples, with KBLaM memory increasing beyond that point.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention equations, training objective and complexity arguments are unchanged. The corrected key/value symbol in Figure 2a's caption is a notation correction, and proposed future tree/graph structures do not introduce a formal derivation or theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about knowledge-token encoding, linear scaling, dynamic updates, interpretable retrieval and question answering. The added code-access statement is a reproducibility disclosure rather than a revised core contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix D discusses upfront adapter-training and per-corpus triple-construction costs, their relationship to runtime benefits, and possible extensions using tree or graph structure. The existing limitations concerning distribution shift, compression-related information loss and more sophisticated reasoning remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an explicit code-and-dataset repository link, whereas v1 states dataset release without that access information. Appendix D newly reports approximately 24–48 hours on one 80GB GPU for one-time preparation/training costs. These disclosures do not establish a changed training budget.

R1.justification: v2 adds the prompt-compression survey by Li et al. and discusses Implicit In-context Learning and Vector-ICL, distinguishing their few-shot demonstration focus from factual KB augmentation. Other related-work changes mainly relocate existing discussion or update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Structured-attention discussion moves into Section 2, while multimodal and continuous-augmentation discussion moves to Appendix A. New appendices, acknowledgments, front-matter updates and limited wording clarifications are added; most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 10–11 and relocates some existing figures without changing their plotted results. The former Figure 10 becomes Figure 12. Caption edits correct Figure 2a and explain the already-existing omission of Enron in-context curves in Figure 6a; the tables remain substantively unchanged.

improvement.justification: The BM25 control and entity-name perturbation test strengthen the retrieval evaluation, while the repository link and explicit upfront-cost discussion improve transparency. These gains are useful but bounded: the RAG efficiency comparison measures LLM overhead, and broad claims of lower memory exceed Figure 11's size-dependent advantage. The core method and earlier evidence remain unchanged.
